# New front in US-Iran war escalates as Houthis fire at Saudi oil facilities

*Conflict also spreads to Caspian Sea as Tehran accuses Ukraine of a deadly attack on an Iranian vessel.*

Save

Share

![FILE PHOTO: A Houthi follower looks on, during a pro-Iran demonstration, as the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran continues, in Sanaa, Yemen April 6, 2026. REUTERS/Khaled Abdullah/File Photo](/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/reuters_6a64aaf4-1784982260.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)

A Houthi follower during a protest in Sanaa, Yemen [File: Khaled Abdullah/Reuters]

[![](/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2017-06-08T131939Z_1189275883_RC11B0FE7F20_RTRMADP_3_GULF-QATAR-JAZEERA-1714943623.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458)

By [Al Jazeera Staff](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458), AP and Reuters

Published On 26 Jul 202626 Jul 2026

Tehran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen have fired missiles and drones at two of Saudi Arabia’s most strategically important oil facilities on the Red Sea, in a major escalation of the latest simmering regional conflict to be reignited by the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran.

But the skies over the country at the epicentre of the widening war were quiet for a second successive night, with no new US attacks on Iran reported by Sunday morning.

(photo credit:  AFP via Getty Images)

ByREUTERS

An oil tanker exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after colliding with a naval mine, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)-linked Tasnim news agency reported on Sunday.

Tasnim said the tanker struck the mine after leaving the route designated by Iran in the strategic waterway.

There was no immediate official statement from Iranian authorities regarding the incident.

[Ukraine](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/22/europe/ukraine-new-military-chief-zelensky-drapatyi-intl) has seen the highest number of civilian casualties in the war with [Russia](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/16/europe/russia-ukraine-kostyantynivka-capture-claim-intl) this month for more than four years, according to government figures.

Russian attacks this month have killed at least 377 civilians and injured 2,129, making it the deadliest month of the war since April 2022.

The attacks this month have included a high number of ballistic missiles, which are difficult to intercept, and have targeted the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, on multiple occasions.

Russia has used nearly 1,700 drones, more than 1,630 guided aerial bombs, and more than 50 ballistic missiles in the last week, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“We must undercut Russia’s gamble on ballistic terror,” Zelensky said in a post on [X](https://x.com/ZelenskyyUa/status/2081283464041492595?s=20) Sunday.

# TSMC Stock And 2 Asian AI Exporters Worth Watching Now

[Simply Wall St](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news)

Surging oil prices near US$100 per barrel, rising global bond yields, and a tense run up to major central bank decisions are putting interest rate expectations back in focus, while AI driven export growth in Asia is supporting a different kind of story for technology exporters. For investors watching South Korean and Taiwanese stocks tied to AI, semiconductors, and hardware, this mix of inflation worries and export strength creates both potential openings and clear risks. This article unpacks how that backdrop connects to three stocks exposed to these trends and what to watch before deciding whether they deserve a place on your radar.

[## Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TWSE:2330)](https://www.simplywall.st/stocks/tw/semiconductors/twse-2330/taiwan-semiconductor-manufacturing-shares?bpId=4674386&link_type=company_1_cta_header)

**Overview:** Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is the world’s largest contract chip manufacturer, producing advanced integrated circuits for clients across high performance computing, smartphones, automotive, Internet of Things, and consumer electronics markets from its global network of fabs and packaging facilities.

**Operations:** TSMC generates essentially all of its NT$4,440,492.3m revenue from its foundry business, manufacturing wafers and related semiconductor processes for external customers.

**Market Cap:** NT$60,94
